    Pseudo-Hermitian Geometry

    Preliminaries

    Edit

    Let \(M^{2m+1}\) be a \((2m+1)\)-dimensional smooth orientable manifold. A CR structure on \(M^{2m+1}\) is a complex rank-\(m\) subbundle \(H^{1,0} \) of \( T(M)\otimes \mathbb{C}\) with the following properties

    \begin{align} H^{1,0} \cap H^{0,1} =& \{0\}, \quad H^{0,1} = \overline{H^{1,0} } \notag \\ [\Gamma (H^{1,0} ),\Gamma (H^{1,0} )] \subseteq &\, \Gamma(H^{1,0} ). \label{1.1} \end{align}

    The complex subbundle \(H^{1,0} \) corresponds to a real rank \(2m\) subbundle \(H :=\Re\{H^{1,0} \oplus H^{0,1} \}\) of \(T(M)\), which carries a complex structure \(J_{b}\) defined by

    \begin{equation*} J_{b}(V+\overline{V})=i(V-\overline{V}) \end{equation*}

    for any \(V\in H^{1,0} \). The synthetic object \((M,H^{1,0} )\) or \( (M,H ,J_{b})\) is called a CR manifold.

    Remark
    Edit

    Formally integrable condition is equivalent to

    \[ \begin{gathered} {\left[J_{b} X, Y\right]+\left[X, J_{b} Y\right] \in \Gamma^{\infty}(U, H(M)),} \\ {\left[J_{b} X, J_{b} Y\right]-[X, Y]=J_{b}\left\{\left[J_{b} X, Y\right]+\left[X, J_{b} Y\right]\right\}} \end{gathered} \]

    for all \(X, Y \in \mathfrak{X}_{\mathcal{H}}\).

    Let \(E\) be a real line bundle of \(T^{\ast }M\), whose fiber at each point \( x\in M\) is given by

    \begin{equation*} E_{x}=\{\omega \in T_{x}^{\ast }M:\ker \omega \supseteq H_{x} \}. \end{equation*}

    Since both \(TM\) and \(H \) are orientable vector bundles on \(M\), the real line bundle \(E\) is orientable, so \(E\) has globally defined nowhere vanishing sections. Any such a section \(\theta \in \Gamma (E\backslash \{0\})\) is referred to as a pseudo-Hermitian 1-form on \(M\).

    Given a pseudo-Hermitian \(1\)-form \(\theta \) on \(M\), we have the Levi form \( L_{\theta }\) corresponding to \(\theta \), which is defined by

    \begin{equation} L_{\theta }(X,Y)=d\theta (X,J_{b}Y) \label{1.2} \end{equation}

    for any \(X,Y\in H \). The second condition in (??) implies that \( L_{\theta }\) is \(J_{b}\)-invariant, and thus symmetric. If \(L_{\theta }\) is positive definite on \(H \) for some \(\theta \), \((M,H^{1,0} )\) is said to be strictly pseudoconvex. From now on, we will always assume that \( (M,H^{1,0} )\) is a strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold endowed with a pseudo-Hermitian \(1\)-form \(\theta \), such that its Levi form \(L_{\theta }\) is positive definite. In this case the synthetic object \((M,H^{1,0} ,\theta )\) is referred to as a pseudo-Hermitian manifold.

    Remark
    Edit

    For any \(Z,W \in H^{1,0}(M)\),

    \[ L_{\theta}(Z, \overline{W})=-i(d \theta)(Z, \overline{W}):=G_{\theta }(Z, \overline{W}). \]

    Let \((M^{2m+1},H^{1,0} , \theta )\) be a pseudo-Hermitian manifold. Clearly \( \theta \) is a contact form. Thus there is a unique vector field \(\xi \in \Gamma (T(M))\), called the Reeb vector field, such that

    \begin{equation} \theta (\xi )=1\quad i_{\xi }d\theta =0 , \label{1.3} \end{equation}

    where \(i_{\xi }\) denotes the interior product with respect to \(\xi \). The collection of all its integral curves forms an oriented one-dimensional foliation \(\mathcal{F}_{\xi }\) on \(M\), which is called the Reeb foliation. The first condition in (??) implies that \(\xi \) is transversal to \(H \). Therefore \(T(M)\) admits a decomposition

    \begin{equation} T(M)=H \oplus V_{\xi }, \label{1.4} \end{equation}

    where \(V_{\xi }:= \mathbb{R} \xi \) is a trivial line bundle on \(M\). In terms of terminology from foliation theory, \(H \) and \(V_{\xi }\) are called the horizontal and vertical distributions respectively. Let \(\pi _{H}:TM\rightarrow H \) and \( \pi _{V}:TM\rightarrow V_{\xi }\) be the natural projections associated with the direct sum decomposition (??). In terms of \(\theta \), the Levi form \(L_{\theta }\) can be extended to a Riemannian metric

    \begin{equation} g_{\theta }=L_{\theta }(\pi _{H},\pi _{H})+\theta \otimes \theta, \label{1.5} \end{equation}

    which is called the Webster metric. It is convenient to extend the complex structure \(J_{b}\) on \(H \) to an endomorphism \(J\) of \(T(M)\) by requiring that

    \begin{equation} J\mid _{H }=J_{b}~\text{ and }~J\mid _{V_{\xi }}=0 , \label{1.6} \end{equation}

    where \(\mid \) denotes the fiberwise restriction. Define the \(2\)-form \(\Omega\) by

    \begin{equation} \Omega(X,Y):=g_{\theta}(X,JY)=-d \theta (X,Y). \end{equation}

    It is known that there exists a unique linear connection \(\nabla \) on \( (M^{2m+1},H^{1,0} ,\theta )\), called the Tanaka-Webster connection, such that (cf. [DT2006differential], [TA1975adifferential], [We1978pseudo])

    1. \(\nabla _{X}\Gamma (H )\subseteq \Gamma (H )\) and \(\nabla _{X}J=0\) for any \(X\in \Gamma (TM)\);

    2. \(\nabla g_{\theta }=0\);

    3. \(T_{\nabla }(X,Y)=2d\theta (X,Y)\xi \) \ and \(T_{\nabla }(\xi ,JX)+JT_{\nabla }(\xi ,X)=0\) for any \(X,Y\in H \), where \(T_{\nabla }(\cdot ,\cdot )\) denotes the torsion of the connection \(\nabla \).

    Note that (3) is equivalent to that \(T_{\nabla }\) is pure(compared to Chern connection), that is,

    \[ \begin{aligned} T_{\nabla }(Z,W)=&0,\\ T_{\nabla }(Z,\overline{W})=& 2 i L_{\theta }(Z,\overline{W}) \xi ,\\ \tau \circ J+J \circ \tau =&0, \end{aligned} \]

    for any \(Z,W \in H^{1,0}(M)\). See [dongren2024dgpseudo] for more information.

    Remark
    Edit

    One has

    \[ T^{\nabla }(X,Y) = 2 g_{\theta }(JX,Y) \xi +\theta (X) \tau Y-\theta (Y) \tau X, \]

    or (be careful with the wedge convention)

    \[ T_{\nabla }=2(\theta \wedge \tau -\Omega \otimes \xi ) .\]

    Also,

    \[ \tau \circ J+J \circ \tau =0; \]

    \[ J^2 Y=-Y+\theta (Y) \xi , \quad \forall Y \in T(M); \]

    \[ [\xi ,X] \in \mathfrak{X}_{H}, \quad \forall X \in \mathfrak{X}_H.\]

    One important partial component of \(T_{\nabla }\) is the pseudo-Hermitian torsion \(\tau \) given by

    \begin{equation} \tau (X)=T_{\nabla }(\xi ,X) \label{1.7} \end{equation}

    for any \(X\in TM\). Then \((M,H^{1,0} ,\theta )\) is said to be Sasakian if \(\tau =0\).

    For the pseudo-Hermitian manifold \((M,H^{1,0} ,\theta )\), we choose a local orthonormal frame field \(\{e_{A}\}_{A=0}^{2m}=\{\xi ,e_{1},...,e_{m},e_{m+1},...,e_{2m}\}\) with respect to \(g_{\theta }\) such that

    \begin{equation*} \{e_{m+1},...,e_{2m}\}=\{Je_{1},...,Je_{m}\}. \end{equation*}

    Such a frame field \(\{e_{A}\}_{A=0}^{2m}\) is referred to as an adapted frame field \(M\). Set

    \begin{equation} \eta _{j}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left( e_{j}-\sqrt{-1}Je_{j}\right) , \quad \eta _{\bar{j}}=\overline{\eta _{j}} \quad (j=1,...,m). \label{1.8} \end{equation}

    Let \(\{\theta ^{j}\}_{j =1}^{m}\) be the dual frame field of \(\{\eta _{j}\}_{j=1}^{m}\). By the properties of the Tanaka-Webster connection \( \nabla \), we have (cf. [DT2006differential])

    \begin{equation} \nabla \xi =0, \quad\nabla \eta _{j}=\theta _{j}^{i}\otimes \eta _{i} \quad \nabla \eta _{\overline{j}}=\theta _{\overline{j}}^{\overline{i} }\otimes \eta _{\overline{i}} , \label{1.9} \end{equation}

    where \(\{\theta _{j}^{i}\}\) denotes the connection \(1\)-forms with respect to the frame field. Since

    \[\tau (H^{1,0} )\subset H^{0,1} ,\]

    one may write

    \begin{eqnarray} \tau &=&\tau ^{i}\eta _{i}+\tau ^{\overline{i}}\eta _{\overline{i}} \notag \\ &=&A_{\overline{j}}^{i}\theta ^{\overline{j}}\otimes \eta _{i}+A_{j}^{ \overline{i}}\theta ^{j}\otimes \eta _{\overline{i}}. \label{1.10} \end{eqnarray}

    Remark
    Edit

    Set

    \[ A(X,Y)=g_{\theta }(\tau X,Y) \]

    for any \(X,Y \in T(M) .\) Then we have \(A(X,Y)=A(Y,X)\). Writing \(A_{ij}=A(\eta_i,\eta_j)\) and \(h_{i \bar j}=g_{\theta }(\eta_i,\eta_{\bar j})\), then

    \[A_{ij}=A_{i}^{\bar k}h_{\bar k j}.\]

    From [We1978pseudo], we know that \(\{\theta ,\theta ^{i},\theta_{j}^{i}\}\) satisfy the following structure equations (cf. also \S 1.4 in [DT2006differential] )

    \begin{eqnarray} d\theta &=&2\sqrt{-1}\theta ^{i}\wedge \theta ^{\overline{i}}\text{,} \notag \\ d\theta ^{i} &=&-\theta _{j}^{i}\wedge \theta ^{j}+A_{\bar{j} }^{i}\theta \wedge \theta ^{\overline{j}}\text{,} \label{1.11} \\ d\theta _{j}^{i} &=&-\theta _{k}^{i}\wedge \theta _{j}^{k}+\Pi _{j}^{i} \notag \end{eqnarray}

    with

    \begin{eqnarray} \Pi _{j}^{i} &=&2\sqrt{-1}(\theta ^{i}\wedge \tau ^{\overline{j}}-\tau ^{i}\wedge \theta ^{\overline{j}})+R_{jk\bar{l}}^{i}\theta ^{k}\wedge \theta ^{\overline{l}} \notag \\ &&+W_{j\overline{k}}^{i}\theta \wedge \theta ^{\overline{k} }-W_{jk}^{i}\theta \wedge \theta ^{k} , \label{1.12} \end{eqnarray}

    where \(W_{j\overline{k}}^{i}=A_{\overline{k},j}^{i}\), \(W_{jk}^{i}=A_{j, \overline{i}}^{\overline{k}}\) are the covariant derivatives of \(A\) and \(R_{jk \bar{l}}^{i}\) are the components of curvature tensor of the Tanaka-Webster connection.

    Lemma ([CDRY2019onharm])
    Edit

    Let \((M^{2m+1},H,J,\theta )\) be a pseudo-Hermitian manifold with Tanaka-Webster connection \(\nabla \). Let \(X\) and \(\rho \) be a vector field and \(1\)-form on \(M\) respectively. Then

    \begin{equation*} \di X=\sum_{A=0}^{2m}g_{\theta }(\nabla _{e_{A}}X,e_{A})~\text{ and }~\delta \rho =-\sum_{A=0}^{2m}(\nabla _{e_{A}}\rho )(e_{A}), \end{equation*}

    where \(\{e_{A}\}_{A=0}^{2m}=\{\xi ,e_{1},...,e_{2m}\}\) is an orthonormal frame field on \(M\). Here \(\di(\cdot )\) and \(\delta (\cdot )\) denote the divergence and codifferential respectively.

    Proposition (Relation with Levi-Civita connection)
    Edit

    Let \(\nabla ^{\theta }\) be the Levi-Civita connection of Webster metric, then

    \begin{equation} \nabla ^{\theta }=\nabla +(\Omega -A) \xi +\tau \otimes \theta +2 \theta \odot J \end{equation}

    and

    \begin{equation}\label{15} \trace_{g_{\theta }}(\nabla ^{\theta }-\nabla )=\trace_{G_{\theta }}(\nabla ^{\theta }-\nabla )=0. \end{equation}

    For curvature tensor, we have

    \[ \begin{aligned} R^\theta(X, Y) Z=R(X, Y) & Z+(L X \wedge L Y) Z-2 \Omega(X, Y) J Z \\ & -g_\theta(S(X, Y), Z) \xi +\theta(Z) S(X, Y) \\ & -2 g_\theta((\theta \wedge \mathcal{O})(X, Y), Z) \xi +2 \theta(Z)(\theta \wedge \mathcal{O})(X, Y), \end{aligned} \]

    for any \(X,Y,Z \in TM\). where

    \[ S(X,Y)=(\nabla _{X}\tau )Y-(\nabla _{Y}\tau )X ,\]

    \[ \mathcal{O}=\tau ^2+2J \tau -I ,\quad L:=\nabla ^{\theta } \xi =\tau +J.\]

    Remark
    Edit

    One has

    \[ \nabla ^{\theta }_{\xi }\xi =0, \qquad \di \xi =0. \]

    Proposition
    Edit

    The Levi distribution \(H(M)\) is minimal and

    \[ \trace (\tau) =0. \]

    Divergence formulas

    Edit
    Definition
    Edit

    Define the divergence of a vector \(X \in TM\) by

    \[ \di (X) \Psi = \mathcal{L}_{X} \Psi ,\]

    where \(\Psi =\theta \wedge (d \theta )^n\) is the volume form and \(\mathcal{L}\) is the Lie derivative.

    Remark
    Edit

    By \eqref{15} and metricity of \(\nabla \),

    \[ \begin{aligned} \di (X)= &\trace_{g_{\theta }}\{Y \in TM \to \nabla^{\theta } _{Y}X\}\\ = &\trace_{g_{\theta }}\{Y \in TM \to \nabla _{Y}X\}. \end{aligned} \]

    Note that

    \[ \begin{aligned} g_{\theta }(\nabla ^{\theta }_{e_{A}}X,e_{A})= g_{\theta }(\nabla ^{\theta }_{\eta _{i }}X,\eta _{\bar i })+g_{\theta }(\nabla ^{\theta }_{\eta _{\bar i }}X,\eta _{ i })+g_{\theta }(\nabla ^{\theta }_{\xi }X,\xi ). \end{aligned} \]

    Exercise
    Edit

    For any complex vector \(Z \in T_{\cc}(M)\),

    \[ \overline{\di (Z)}=\di (\bar{Z}) .\]

    Definition
    Edit

    Define the divergence of a 1-form \(\sigma \) by

    \[ \di (\sigma )=\di (X_{\sigma }), \]

    where \(X_{\sigma }\) is the dual vector of \(\sigma \) w.r.t. \(g_{\theta }\), i.e., \(g_{\theta }(X_{\sigma },Y)=\sigma (Y), \forall ~ Y \in T(M) \).

    Exercise
    Edit

    For any \( Z=Z^{i }e_{i }\in H^{1,0}(M)\), we have

    \[ \di (Z)=e_{i }(Z^{i })+Z^{j } \theta_{j }^{i }(e_{i }). \]

    If \(\sigma =\sigma _i \theta ^i\), then

    \[ \di (\sigma )=\sigma _{i ,\bar{j }}h^{i \bar{j }}. \]

    Definition
    Edit

    Sub-Laplacian for a smooth function \(u\) is defined by

    \[ \Delta _b(u):=\di(\nabla^{h} u)=u_{i \bar{j }}h^{i \bar{j }}+u_{\bar{i }j }h^{\bar{i }j },\]

    where \(\nabla ^{h}u\) is the horizontal component of the gradient \(\nabla u\).

    Note that

    \[ \nabla ^h u = u_{i} e_{\bar i}+u_{\bar i} e_{i}. \]

    Exercise
    Edit

    The usual Laplacian is given by

    \[ \Delta u= u_{i \bar{j }}h^{i \bar{j }}+u_{\bar{i }j }h^{\bar{i }j }+u_{00}. \]

    Proposition (Stokes' formulas)
    Edit

    If at least one of the smooth functions \(a,b\) has compact support, then

    \begin{equation}\label{eq:laplacian-symmetry} \begin{aligned} \int_Ma\,\Delta b\dd&=-\int_M\ip{da}{db}\dd=\int_Mb\,\Delta a\dd,\\ \int_Ma\,\Delta_bb\dd&=-\int_M\ip{d_Ha}{d_Hb}\dd,\\ \int_Ma\,\xi^2b\dd&=-\int_M(\xi a)(\xi b)\dd . \end{aligned} \end{equation}

    Proposition
    Edit

    Put \(D=\nabla ^{\theta }\) and

    \begin{equation}\label{eq:Z-def} \mathsf Z=\Delta^{D }\xi+\ricci_g^\sharp\xi,\qquad \Delta^D=\sum_\mu\bigl(D_{e_\mu}D_{e_\mu}-D_{D_{e_\mu}e_\mu}\bigr), \end{equation}

    where \(\ricci_g^\sharp\) is the Ricci endomorphism of \(g\), and \(\di_g\tau=\sum_\mu(D_{e_\mu}\tau)e_\mu\). Then

    \begin{equation}\label{eq:z-div} \mathsf Z=2\di_g\tau, \end{equation}

    and for horizontal \(X\),

    \begin{equation}\label{eq:reeb-curvature} R^{\theta }(X,\xi)\xi=X-2J\tau X-\tau^2X-(\nabla_\xi\tau)X . \end{equation}

    Curvatures

    Edit
    Definition
    Edit

    The Ricci tensor of the Webster connection is defined by

    \[ \operatorname{Ric}(Y,Z) = \operatorname{trace}\{X\mapsto R(X,Z)Y\}, \]

    for any \(Y,Z\in T(M)\). The pseudo-Hermitian Ricci tensor is then given by

    \[ R_{i\bar{j}} = \operatorname{Ric}(\eta _i,\eta _{\bar{j}}). \]

    Let us set

    \[ R_{i\bar{j}k\bar{l}} = g_{\theta}\bigl(R(\eta_k,\eta_{\bar{l}})\eta_i,\eta_{\bar{j}}\bigr) = h_{s\bar{j}}\,R^{s}_{ik\bar{l}}, \]

    where \(R\) is the curvature tensor of \(\nabla\). One may derive that (cf.~[DT2006differential])

    \[ R_{i\bar{j}k\bar{l}}=R_{k\bar{j}i\bar{l}}. \]

    The pseudo-Hermitian Ricci tensor is given by

    \[ R_{k\bar{l}} = R^{i}_{ki\bar{l}} = R^{i}_{ik\bar{l}}, \]

    which satisfies

    \[ R_{k\bar{l}}=R_{\bar{l}k}. \]

    Since the Tanaka--Webster connection can be viewed as a connection in \(H^{1,0}(M)\), the pseudo-Hermitian Ricci tensor and the torsion tensor on \(H^{1,0}(M)\) are also denoted by

    \[ \operatorname{Ric}(X,Y)=R_{i\bar{j}}X^{i}Y^{\bar{j}} \]

    and

    \[ \operatorname{Tor}(X,Y) = \sqrt{-1}\bigl(A_{\bar{i}\bar{j}}X^{\bar{i}}Y^{\bar{j}}-A_{ij}X^{i}Y^{j}\bigr) \]

    for any \(X=X^{i}\eta _i\), \(Y=Y^{j}\eta _j\in H^{1,0}(M)\).
